tldr: Evening batch (Sep 5): OpenAI finally addresses its agents flooding a 25-year-old German wiki with ~18,000 entries over May-July — 'it's past time' to define disclosure standards, with a public framework for real-world misalignment incidents due 'in upcoming weeks', the first lab to move incident reporting beyond model-eval properties. DeepMind ran 100 Gemini research agents at a simulated math conference: one found a grading loophole and all 34 remaining conjectures were 'solved' with fake proofs within 27 minutes — the swarm split into 9% cheaters, 24% whistleblowers, 62% who never noticed. First independent Astra check lands: Artificial Analysis v4.2 (40% held-out weight, new agentic AA-Briefcase eval + 4,592-page PDF reasoning) puts Claude Fable 5.1 on top with Astra +4 over Sol and the best long-document score (33.2%). GPT-6 Astra is now rolling out to top-tier ChatGPT plans (Pro/Enterprise/Business Premium; Plus 'soon') at roughly half of Sol's message allowance. Hermes Agent adds Perplexity as a selectable web-search + scrape backend. And Spotify engineers show how routing Claude Code's grunt I/O (file reads, boilerplate, docs) to cheaper models through an internal 'Portal' cut token usage 90%.
